item.title: Fraud Losses Hit Record $15.9 Billion: The Surprising 2026 Reality
item.description:
Americans lost a staggering $15.9 billion to fraud in 2025 — a record-shattering figure that exposes just how aggressive, organized, and digitally savvy today’s scammers have become. If you think fraud is somebody else’s problem, the latest numbers from the Federal Trade Commission suggest otherwise.

Key Takeaways

  • Consumer fraud losses hit a record $15.9 billion in 2025, up from $12.5 billion in 2024 (FTC).
  • Investment scams alone accounted for nearly half — $7.9 billion.
  • Imposter scams generated more than 1 million reports and $3.5 billion in losses.
  • The SBA referred 562,000 suspected fraudulent pandemic loans worth $22.2 billion to Treasury for collection in April 2026.
  • Reported fraud losses have surged nearly 430% since 2020.

The scope of fraud in America has shifted dramatically in just five years. What used to be isolated cons targeting the elderly has become a multibillion-dollar industry blending text messages, social media, and impersonation tactics that fool people of every age group. Below, we unpack the numbers — and what they actually mean for your wallet.

item.title: Crypto ATM Scams Cost Americans $333 Million — What You Need to Know
item.description:
Did you know the average victim of a crypto ATM scam is 73 years old and loses roughly $17,000 in a single transaction? That’s not a hypothetical — it’s a real statistic from fraud investigators in Manchester, New Hampshire, and it’s part of a national crisis that’s finally forcing lawmakers to act.

Key Takeaways:

  • The FBI reported $333.5 million in crypto ATM scam losses from January to November 2025 — up from $250 million in 2024.
  • Indiana became the first state to ban crypto kiosks outright, sidelining roughly 800 machines.
  • The global crypto ATM count has dropped to 38,928 after a net loss of 597 machines in Q1 2026.
  • New Hampshire, West Virginia, and Arizona are advancing new consumer protection legislation.

Crypto ATM Fraud Is Surging Across the United States

The numbers are staggering. According to the FBI, fraudsters stole $333.5 million from Americans through bitcoin ATM scams between January and November 2025. That figure represents a 33% increase over the roughly $250 million lost in 2024, which itself was more than double the previous year’s total.
